name: Microbiology PhD
summary: A PhD in the UW Department of Microbiology. You apply to the program, rotate through three labs for 10 weeks each in your first year, and choose a thesis lab in spring quarter.

deadlines.label: Application deadline
deadlines.note: The department's admission page gives an application period of September 1 to December 1 for domestic and international applicants and lists December 1 as the deadline. The UW Graduate School's program listing shows 12/01/2026 for Autumn 2027, domestic and international. The department recommends that international applicants apply by November 1. No time of day is stated for this program.

timeline.interviews: Interviews are by invitation only and are normally held in late January or early February.
timeline.decisions: Offers of admission are generally released 3 to 4 weeks after the interviews.

english.note: The department page lists the English tests for international applicants and points to the UW Graduate School rules, which ask every applicant whose native language isn't English for a qualifying degree taught in English (Policy 3.2) or a test score. These are the Graduate School minimums; below them an application isn't considered. TOEFL 4.5 (92 for earlier tests), IELTS 7.0 or Duolingo 130 or higher meet the requirement without conditions; admitted students scoring lower must take UW Academic English courses. Duolingo: the requirements page says 110 (recommended 125), Policy 3.2 says 115 (recommended 130); the higher figures are shown. Scores are valid for two years.

applicationFee.note: The fee is set by the UW Graduate School and each application needs its own fee. The department says waivers come through the Graduate School for domestic students on a needs basis and are not available for international students; the Graduate School's waiver is for U.S. citizens, permanent residents and undocumented applicants (and McNair Scholars and PPIA Fellows), not for F-1 or J-1 applicants. The department also asks you to email its graduate program adviser (microgpa@uw.edu) about waivers and says funding decides whether it can offer any. Ask at least seven days before the deadline.

documents: Unofficial transcripts uploaded in the application (no paper copies)
Short-answer questions, used instead of a personal statement
requirements.note: Interviews are by invitation only. The department strongly recommends undergraduate courses in biochemistry, physics, general and organic chemistry, microbiology, molecular biology and cell biology, and undergraduate research. You must have a bachelor's or advanced degree by the time you start. Study is full time only, and there is no master's program. You don't need to contact professors before applying.

funding.note: Most students are paid as research assistants from departmental funds in their first year; after that, depending on funding, by their advisor's grants, a training grant or a fellowship. Assistantships carry a monthly stipend, a tuition waiver and health benefits, and students pay a student activity fee each quarter. The FAQ says international students are often not eligible for training grants and fellowships, and that a teaching assistantship can't be awarded to foreign applicants unless they scored above 580 on the TOEFL (the page's own wording). No stipend amount is stated.

international.note: The application period and the December 1 deadline are the same for domestic and international applicants; the department recommends that international applicants apply by November 1.
